Comments (English): I already had a dish dryer, so I deliberated for a long time before finally deciding on a Samsung product because of its great value. So, I brought home a dishwasher lady this time. Product Color: They said it was white, but it isn't white. Anyway, it has a grayish tint. Product Design: It has a simple rectangular, square shape. The front is finished with tempered glass, making it very simple yet luxurious. Service/Installation: Two Samsung technicians came and installed it very kindly. I am very satisfied. Functions: I haven't actually used it yet, but the technician drove it briefly and it worked very well. I need to pile up some dishes quickly to give it a try. The 12-place setting is spacious, so it seems like it will be very good for washing dishes. However, there are comments saying that while a 12-place dishwasher is good for large loads, it can be difficult to run when the amount is small. I also thought it might be inconvenient during a move. I am satisfied with this product because of the price and the fact that I can wash small loads without feeling burdened. (For reference, I am a family of four.) Conclusion: It used to be stressful when I was busy and the amount of dishes piled up. Many people say that hiring a dishwasher "Auntie" is a whole new world, so I decided to get one. I hope that thanks to her, I can finally escape some stress. ~ After 2 weeks of use. Noise: Some people say the running sound is loud, but you should expect it to be about the same as a washing machine. The noise level when draining the water is almost on par with a washing machine. With a washing machine, you can keep it in the laundry room and close the door so you don't hear it running, but since a dishwasher is placed in the kitchen, you have to accept the noise with your whole ears. If dishes are placed upside down or standing upright like plates, or if spoons and chopsticks are cleaned well, but if dishes are stacked, the cleaning isn't perfect and water pools, so I have to take them out, wash them again, and dry them in the dryer. Overall Impression: I hired a dishwasher "Auntie" for convenience, but the washing time is a bit slow, and since she doesn't clean the dishes perfectly, it requires a bit of extra effort. ~ I guess I'll have to make do with this until a dishwasher comes out that addresses these downsides (noise, perfect cleaning, and washing time). ~
Comments (Original): 기존에 식기건조기가 있어서 고심고심하다가 이번에 삼성 가성비 좋은 제품이라이번에 식기세척기 이모님 모셔왔습니다.제품색 : 화이트라고 했는데 화이트는 아니구요. 여튼 회색빛입니다. 제품디자인 : 심플한 사각형 정사각형의 모양 앞면은 강화유리 처리로 매우 심플하고 고급스럽습니다.서비스 설치 : 두 분의 삼성기사분이 오셔서 아주매우 친절하게 설치해주셨습니다. 매우 만족입니다.기능 : 아직 진행은 안해보았으나, 기사분이 잠깐 운행해 주셨는데 매우 좋은 상태로 진행되었습니다.설겆이감을 빨리 쌓아서 해보아야겠습니다.12인이 넓어서 식기세척하기는 매우 좋을 듯 하나, 식기세척기 12인은 양이 많을 때는 좋기는 하지만 양이 적을 때 돌리기는 그럴 때가 있다고 하는 댓글이 있고 이사시에 불편할 것 같기도 하고 이 제품은 가격부분 이나 적은 양도 부담스럽지 않게 세척할 수 있어서 만족합니다.(참고로 가족 4인입니다.)결론 : 바쁠 때 설겆이 양이 쌓일 때 스트레스가 되더라구요. 식기세척기 이모님 모셔오면 너무 너무 신세계라는 분들이 많아서 이번에 들여놓았는데 이모님 덕분에 스트레스에서 벗어날 수 있기를 바래보아요. ~ ㅎ2주일 사용 후소리 : 세척기 돌아가는 소리가 크다고 하시는 분들도 있는데 세탁기 소리 정도 난다 생각하시면 됩니다. 식기세척기 물 배출시 거의 세탁기 수준의 소음입니다. 세탁기의 경우는 세탁실에 넣어두고 문을 닫아 세탁기 돌아가는 소리가 들리지 않지만 식기세척기는 주방쪽에 놓고 사용하는 것이라 소음을 온 귀로 받아들여야 합니다. 그릇을 뒤집어 놓거나 접시처럼 세워 놓는 경우, 그리고 숟가락 젖가락은 잘 닦이나, 그릇이 겹쳐지는 경우는 세척도 완벽하게 되지 않고 물이 고여있거나 하기에 다시 한번 꺼내 씻고 건조기에 말립니다. 총평 : 편하려고 식기세척기 이모님 모셔왔는데 설겆이 시간이 좀 느린 편이시고, 완벽하게 식기를 세척해 주시지 않아 손이 좀 가는 편입니다. ~ 단점들(소리, 완벽한 세척, 세척시간)을 보완한 식기세척기가 나올 때까지 아쉬운대로 사용해야 겠네요. ~

Functions: I haven't actually used it yet, but the technician drove it briefly and it worked very well. I need to pile up some dishes quickly to give it a try. The 12-place setting is spacious, so it seems like it will be very good for washing dishes. However, there are comments saying that while a 12-place dishwasher is good for large loads, it can be difficult to run when the amount is small. I also thought it might be inconvenient during a move. I am satisfied with this product because of the price and the fact that I can wash small loads without feeling burdened. (For reference, I am a family of four.) Conclusion: It used to be stressful when I was busy and the amount of dishes piled up. Many people say that hiring a dishwasher "Auntie" is a whole new world, so I decided to get one. I hope that thanks to her, I can finally escape some stress. ~ After 2 weeks of use. Noise: Some people say the running sound is loud, but you should expect it to be about the same as a washing machine. The noise level when draining the water is almost on par with a washing machine. With a washing machine, you can keep it in the laundry room and close the door so you don't hear it running, but since a dishwasher is placed in the kitchen, you have to accept the noise with your whole ears. If dishes are placed upside down or standing upright like plates, or if spoons and chopsticks are cleaned well, but if dishes are stacked, the cleaning isn't perfect and water pools, so I have to take them out, wash them again, and dry them in the dryer. Overall Impression: I hired a dishwasher "Auntie" for convenience, but the washing time is a bit slow, and since she doesn't clean the dishes perfectly, it requires a bit of extra effort. ~ I guess I'll have to make do with this until a dishwasher comes out that addresses these downsides (noise, perfect cleaning, and washing time). ~

Comments (English): I already had a dish dryer, so I deliberated for a long time before finally deciding on a Samsung product because of its great value. So, I brought home a dishwasher lady this time. Product Color: They said it was white, but it isn't white. Anyway, it has a grayish tint. Product Design: It has a simple rectangular, square shape. The front is finished with tempered glass, making it very simple yet luxurious. Service/Installation: Two Samsung technicians came and installed it very kindly. I am very satisfied. Functions: I haven't actually used it yet, but the technician drove it briefly and it worked very well. I need to pile up some dishes quickly to give it a try. The 12-place setting is spacious, so it seems like it will be very good for washing dishes. However, there are comments saying that while a 12-place dishwasher is good for large loads, it can be difficult to run when the amount is small. I also thought it might be inconvenient during a move. I am satisfied with this product because of the price and the fact that I can wash small loads without feeling burdened. (For reference, I am a family of four.) Conclusion: It used to be stressful when I was busy and the amount of dishes piled up. Many people say that hiring a dishwasher "Auntie" is a whole new world, so I decided to get one. I hope that thanks to her, I can finally escape some stress. ~ After 2 weeks of use. Noise: Some people say the running sound is loud, but you should expect it to be about the same as a washing machine. The noise level when draining the water is almost on par with a washing machine. With a washing machine, you can keep it in the laundry room and close the door so you don't hear it running, but since a dishwasher is placed in the kitchen, you have to accept the noise with your whole ears. If dishes are placed upside down or standing upright like plates, or if spoons and chopsticks are cleaned well, but if dishes are stacked, the cleaning isn't perfect and water pools, so I have to take them out, wash them again, and dry them in the dryer. Overall Impression: I hired a dishwasher "Auntie" for convenience, but the washing time is a bit slow, and since she doesn't clean the dishes perfectly, it requires a bit of extra effort. ~ I guess I'll have to make do with this until a dishwasher comes out that addresses these downsides (noise, perfect cleaning, and washing time). ~

Comments (English): [ Example of installing a countertop dishwasher into the cooker valve hole ] || ---------------- || I've attached photos, so please take a look and compare! In my case, I have a kitchen water purifier next to the sink that wasn't in use and was just sitting there, so I asked them to install it in that spot. I figured drilling into the sink was better than drilling into the marble! Since there was a small hole left, they didn't fill it up further. (I was actually expecting them to apply silicone, but well, it's where my water purifier used to be, so I understand; I can just fill it in myself.) I ordered it the day before, and they came to install it at 11 AM the next day. Even a Power P-type person like me can get a dishwasher installed the day after moving, as long as I have Coupang. I installed it this way because tearing down the base cabinets and all that was such a headache. Actually, the biggest downside is the space it takes up. It looks a bit cramped, right? I thought I could install it by just removing one base cabinet door, but that wasn't the case. In my case, to fit the size, I would have had to either remove the oven and sterilizer, or do a major renovation by tearing down two base cabinets to fit it. If that were the case, I would have just used a countertop model and waited until the whole house was remodeled. The conclusion was to get a dishwasher. Anyway, after using it, the functions are good. One wash cycle takes about an hour and a half. The sound isn't bothersome; it's about the same noise level as my husband opening the bathroom door and washing his face. It does that for an hour and a half. That's about the level. Unless you are sensitive to noise, you'll just think, "Oh, the dishwasher is running." I think you can just leave it on when you go out. (TMI: I don't really like noise. I wake up in the morning, do housework while doing laundry, and get the kids ready for school. I eat, put all the dishes in the dishwasher, and run it. I set the timer for the robot vacuum to leave, and once the laundry is done, I run the dryer and dishwasher while I go to work. Then, when I get home, I don't have to worry about noise. After dinner, I soak the dishes in water and repeat the process endlessly the next morning.) After the first use, I looked inside after the automatic door opened. The water wasn't completely gone like in the advertisements. There was quite a bit of moisture bubbled up, and it gradually dried naturally. I'm talking about that little book on newsprint in several languages that ships with appliance.

Comments (English): [ Excellent ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) I've only had it a month but I am thrilled with this product. #1 Crystal Dry - Even our plastic lids come fully dry. We no longer have to fill the drainboard with dishes to dry. #2 Other stainless exterior dishwashers I've owned always seemed to have drips I needed to buff away. Any drips on this black stainless seem to just disappear with no wiping. Only the tiny, shiny strip on the handle ever shows smudges or fingerprints. #3 It cleans, even on Auto. In fact it took weeks of us actively trying to find something it couldn't clean (burnt in gnochhi on a frying pan - but even that would have come clean by changing the cycle or laying the pan face down). #4 love the clear indicator that a cycle is still in progress. No more screwing up a wash by opening the door mid-cycle. And we really need that indicator, becuase the wash is soooo quiet. #5 The middle and 3rd rack are particularly well designed. Because the middle rack can adjust height and because of the length and distance between the tines, I can fit so much more onto that 2nd rack, making the whole dishwasher interior seem so much larger. Also, things don't fly around because that middle rack is so thoughtfully designed. That said, I wish the lower rack had more drop down tine flexibility for all our glass lunch containers - which we've been forced to lay perpendicular to the plates. The tines' spaces are either too wide or too narrow to fit things efficiently. #5 We stopped using the cutlery container years ago, but the 3rd rack on this Bosch is next level compared to my experience with other brands. I highly recommend other buyers rethink using those finicky cultery trays in favour of 3rd racks. #6 The rinse-aid and tablet refill warnings were a nice surprise. #7 Easy to read & easy to use setting 'buttons'. This dishwasher was well worth its price. Loading, washing/drying and unloading dishes are no longer a frustration.

Comments (English): [ High-performance, fully installed 6-place setting dishwasher – the best value for money! ] || ---------------- || My apartment is 25 pyeong, which is a bit small. Since I bought the installed model instead of the portable one, it is incredibly convenient because I don't have to add water separately. Even though I live alone, I use water cups so frequently that they pile up in the mornings and evenings, and washing them is actually quite a hassle. I highly recommend getting one if you're a working professional! It feels like I've bought time with money. I can do other things with that time.

The same holders can be found in the height-adjustable middle compartment for glasses and bowls. Here too, the right side can be easily folded down and the cutlery compartment is at a decent height and is easy to put away. The cleaning performance is great and everything gets clean without any problems. Unfortunately, there are spoons in the cutlery compartment. Normal dirt is not a problem, but rice or egg residue is a real problem and doesn't go away. On the whole, however, this is not a problem with a short pre-rinse. The app connection also works great. The only thing that should be communicated in the instructions is that the router must be switched to WPS mode to establish the connection. Unfortunately, this was not communicated and I was only able to find out through the internet. Overall, we are very satisfied and would recommend him without reservation except for the points mentioned!

Im Großen und Ganzen sind wir aber sehr zufrieden und würden Ihn bis auf die genannten Punkte unbeschränkt weiterempfehlen !

Nobody would know that unless you actually read the owner's manual, and who actually does that when the average person has used a dishwasher practically their whole life? Oh! And don't call the customer support line, cause like most tech support people, they'll talk to you like you're some idiot that doesn't know how to operate a dishwasher, after sitting on hold for 10-15 minutes. There have been multiple times since owning this machine that I have had to scrub food off of supposedly clean dishes after running through a cycle in the machine. I would most definitely recommend to do a lot more research on different machines and brands and DEFINITELY read the reviews before deciding and making a purchase.

Comments (English): [ DO NOT BUY! GET READY FOR RUST AND PEELING PLASTIC ] || ---------------- || Bought this a little over a year ago. Called Kitchenaid and expressed my concerns about rust forming where the steam vent is on the outside of the dishwasher. I tried using stainless cleaner and it did not work. I also noticed peeling at the bottom of the unit. I thought the protective plastic was still on it. I tired to pull on the piece sticking out and it came off in a tiny piece and I stopped. The whole bottom is showing lifting, what looks like a plastic coating over the stainless. I called Kitchenaid and spoke to a nice man who set me up with an appliance company to come out and look at it. I get a email and to my shock! It stated I would be responsible for paying for repairs since my product was not under the one year warranty! He never said a word about me having to foot the bill. Why on earth would I use a contracted appliance company through Kitchenaid if it's no longer under warranty. I called Kitchenaid back and spoke to lady and she told me I'd have to pay. I know, I read that! This is a defect! This is not misuse, this is not wear and tear, this is a defective item! She NEVER called me back. Awesome customer service! Call number 3! Spoke to another woman and my first question was, you have my phone number correct? Yes, was her response. Perfect! If the line gets disconnected, please call back. She looked at the account and she basically told me I'm out of luck and wanted to know if I wanted to cancel my appliance repair appointment. Again, why would I use your appliance repair company if I'm footing the bill for a defective product! It's rusting! The plastic over the stainless is peeling. Why is there plastic on this! The dishwasher gets hot! You don't think this coating is going to start to break down? Fail is the design. I paid a lot of money for a product that looks like the cheapest low end dishwasher that's slightly over a year old. She apologized and said, sorry. Kitchenaid, this is a known issue. It's all over the internet. So many people with rusting and peeling dishwashers! How about make it right! Stand behind your product! I could understand if I dented it or scratched it. This dishwasher is in perfect condition, other than the defect of rusting by the steam vent and peeling plastic. Please do the right thing and make this right! I would add pictures, but the add picture is not working. Take my word for it, don't buy this or any Kitchenaid product because they don't stand behind their defective products. Sentence (English): The dishwasher has the features I wanted.
Comments (English): [ I am probably sticking with GE ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher has the features I wanted. But there is no clear information regarding how to use the machine, nor what to expect? Not even a VIDEO with user friendly information for this model. The first test use was good, asking the dishwasher to run a 16 minute rinse cycle. But when I put in a load, I could not get a cycle to show a time for less than 2 hours and 10 minutes. I only wanted a short 1 hour wash. That was not obtainable. Additionally, with the full cycle, I heard some hard popping noise coming from the sink. My plumber (by phone) is assuming there was air in the line. But that is hard to believe, since the 16 minute rinse cycle test did not not have that issue. I cried when the installer pulled out my 31 year old GE dishwasher. The only thing wrong with it was the door pulleys broke. They were replaced one year ago, but the available replacement parts must have been inferior. It is disheartening to know the new dishwasher appears to have the same pulley system. Perhaps this will last 30 years, too? I will miss my original GE dishwasher. Hoping to fall in love with my new GE dishwasher.

Sentence (English): No to KitchenAid, and no to bestbuy!
Comments (English): [ UNPAID/UNREWARDED, HONEST Review RUN!  ] || ---------------- || No to KitchenAid, and no to Best Buy! First, pay attention to these reviews as the majority are incentivize. Dishwasher: We picked it up from the store, brought it home and installed immediately (husband is a plumber). While installing, he mentioned he felt like the dishwasher had been hooked up previously because of how the electrical . connections looked. We discussed maybe it was done at the manufacturer for testing because when we received it, the dishwasher was factory packaged inside what appeared to be the original box. Installation took about 1.5 hrs. Finally, I could now get my hands on this beauty and give it a test run! Opened door, pulled out middle rack and immediately noticed a PLASTIC (this word will be used a lot) clip was missing off one of the adjustable dish holders rendering it unusable because it would not stand up, Refusing to be dismayed, thinking that's a simple fix, sure the manufacturer will just send a replacement and we can easily snap it in, I move on to explore the adjustable rack. Except it will NOT adjust for some reason. Upon further inspection, we find the PLASTIC piece that attached the rack to the right side roller is completely broken off, and that piece is nowhere to be found (not in the bottom of the dishwasher). Speaking of the bottom of the dishwasher—there was sediment in the bottom that looked as if it had been used previously. Frustrated now, but still determined to use this baby until we can get the brand new $1300 dishwasher repaired, I begin the process of running a load. Well, if you are over 25, this one likely is not for you. Hubs and I are both techies. We are in our 50's, but have stayed proficient with technology for the most part. Neither of us could get the thing started, even after consulting the hideous “manual.” Our 23 year old daughter was finally able to get it going, but it was a bit challenging for her as well. The programming is NOT intuitive, and the manual is worthless. It is printed on cheap paper, in fifty languages on the same page, and is very difficult to read and follow. We ran a load, and the results were satisfactory; finally a positive note. We are unsure if we were sold a refurb, that was poorly refurbed, at regular price, OR if KitchenAid's QC is what poor, but the fact this ever left the warehouse with missing and broken parts speaks volumes. The entire dishwasher is composed of a LOT of PLASTIC parts and pieces. That, along with the issues we encountered, led us to be confident we did not want to return for the same brand. The return:. So it begins: first I go online and as recommended under the contact option, I ATTEMPT to CHAT with Customer Service. After forty-five minutes of no answer in chat, I moved on to the next recommendation; text. I waited An hour, received no response, so went to bed. The next morning, they had responded two hours and forty five minutes later. Because I was asleep and didn't answer immediately, they closed that chat. The next morning, I waited until store hours so I could call the local store and speak with someone to give me my options on exchange. We live 30 mins from the store, and we're hoping they would pick up/deliver and maybe uninstall/reinstall the exchange. Welllll, after being disconnected twice because their phone tree takes you in a horrific circle of options, I finally learned the right things to say or buttons to push in order to reach a human…or so I thought. I was At work, so I put the phone on speakerphone and went about my day while holding for a live representative. You're given the option of having them call you back instead of waiting, but I opted to wait the estimated eight minutes instead. Sixteen minutes later, I reach a live representative, but wait…she sounds nothing like people from our area of town. She was super nice, and we both worked hard to get through the language barrier as English was definitely not her first language. After ten minutes with her, she advises she needs to transfer me to someone who can assist with exchanging the product. I think finally I am being transferred to the local store! Hah, NOT! Next a gentleman answers. Again, nice, friendly, and speaking in broken English. I work In healthcare where we interact with various cultures and languages all day long; I am accustomed to accents and rarely do I have problems understanding non-American accents. Well, like the first representative, he had a thick foreign accent that I (and my coworkers) struggled to understand, but we worked through it. The offer: They would send out replacement, and pick up the other one for free! No, they wouldn't uninstall and reinstall. Timeframe on exchange? Two weeks. I thanked him, told him we would just return to the local store and hung up. Husband uninstalls, loads it back in the truck along with all the packaging, and makes the thirty minute trip back to the store. What happens next? We paid cash the day prior, but this very busy (Nov 30th) store claims they do not keep that much cash, so they will have to MAIL us a check. Hubs pushes back and they finally agree to credit to his debit card. I will brag and say the next morning, our cash purchase had been safely returned to our bank account. We went to a different big box store that starts with a “L” and purchased a different brand that starts with a “B” (google—most recommended brand-that started out manufacturing tools, I believe). Paid about $50 more, but it's now installed. Parts seem much more substantial, and not nearly as much PLASTIC. Programming is very intuitive. So, we are fine with Best Buy—will never purchase as much as a computer mouse from them again (and we've been long-term customers), and will NEVER even look at a large KitchenAid appliance again. Do not recommend Best Buy or KitchenAid!

Sentence (English): The sound level is similar to that of a washing machine.

After a lot of homework, I finally picked this model. It is cost-effective. I randomly found a few pot lids with water stains and tried them on. I used the super-fast washing mode. After washing, they became much brighter, but there were still water stains. It is estimated that the washing time is not enough, and the water quality is too hard. Let’s study it carefully after moving in. There are two problems: the ultra-fast mode does not automatically open the door, and the automatic door opening function is on. I bought a Haier dishwasher just for this function. I don’t know why it can’t open the door automatically. 2 After washing, the entire dishwasher was full of water, and it didn’t dry out all afternoon. I don’t know if this is normal.

I really love this dishwasher!

We discussed maybe it was done at the manufacturer for testing because when we received it, the dishwasher was factory packaged inside what appeared to be the original box. Installation took about 1.5 hrs.Finally, I could now get my hands on this beauty and give it a test run! Opened door, pulled out middle rack and immediately noticed a PLASTIC (this word will be used a lot) clip was missing off one of the adjustable dish holders rendering it unusable because it would not stand up, Refusing to be dismayed, thinking that's a simple fix, sure the manufacturer will just send a replacement and we can easily snap it in, I move on to explore the adjustable rack. Except it will NOT adjust for some reason. Upon further inspection, we find the PLASTIC piece that attached the rack to the right side roller is completely broken off, and that piece is nowhere to be found (not in the bottom of the dishwasher). Speaking of the bottom of the dishwasher—there was sediment in the bottom that looked as if it had been used previously. Frustrated now, but still determined to use this baby until we can get the brand new $1300 dishwasher repaired, I begin the process of running a load. Well, if you are over 25, this one likely is not for you. Hubs and I are both techies. We are in our 50's, but have stayed proficient with technology for the most part. Neither of us could get the thing started, even after consulting the hideous “manual.” Our 23 year old daughter was finally able to get it going, but it was a bit challenging for her as well. The programming is NOT intuitive, and the manual is worthless. It is printed on cheap paper, in fifty languages on the same page, and is very difficult to read and follow. We ran a load, and the results were satisfactory; finally a positive note. We are unsure if we were sold a refurb, that was poorly refurbed, at regular price, OR if KitchenAid's QC is what poor, but the fact this ever left the warehouse with missing and broken parts speaks volumes. The entire dishwasher is composed of a LOT of PLASTIC parts and pieces. That, along with the issues we encountered, led us to be confident we did not want to return for the same brand. After forty-five minutes of no answer in chat, I moved on to the next recommendation; text. I waited An hour, received no response, so went to bed. The next morning, they had responded two hours and forty five minutes later. Because I was asleep and didn't answer immediately, they closed that chat. The next morning, I waited until store hours so I could call the local store and speak with someone to give me my options on exchange. We live 30 mins from the store, and we're hoping they would pick up/deliver and maybe uninstall/reinstall the exchange. Welllll, after being disconnected twice because their phone tree takes you in a horrific circle of options, I finally learned the right things to say or buttons to push in order to reach a human…or so I thought. Sixteen minutes later, I reach a live representative, but wait…she sounds nothing like people from our area of town. After ten minutes with her, she advises she needs to transfer me to someone who can assist with exchanging the product. I think finally I am being transferred to the local store! Hah, NOT! Sentence (English): I would be very happy with this dishwasher, but when we open the door, we get a small puddle under the vent on the top left corner.
Comments (English): [ Leaves a wet spot on the floor ] || ---------------- || I would be very happy with this dishwasher, but when we open the door, we get a small puddle under the vent on the top left corner. We have had service to fix it, and the final diagnosis is that "the machine is operating as designed." The official troubleshooting manual says "Water vapor is released through the vent in the door. Sometimes there will be a water spot on the floor after the door has been opened." If we had tile floors, maybe that would be ok, but unless we wipe up the floor after emptying the dishwasher, it damages the wood. Customer service suggested it would be better to empty the dishwasher immediately after the drying cycle, which would mean getting up at 2am. We also had a problem with the control board, which was fixed under warranty, but I would not buy this model again.

Sentence (English): We've had the dishwasher for just three weeks and today the control panel started malfunctioning.
Comments (English): [ Trouble after just 3 weeks - control board ] || ---------------- || We've had the dishwasher for just three weeks and today the control panel started malfunctioning. We were around the kitchen table when, all of a sudden, all sorts of random beep-boop sounds start coming from the dishwasher. It was not running, and just sitting there in “off” mode, with the door slightly ajar. I walked over to take a closer look and not only did the beep-boop sounds continue, but lights all over the control panel were flashing randomly and the LED display which is supposed to show a time remaining (e.g., 3:06) was flashing all sorts or random things, not numbers. I tried pressing “cancel” to stop but it just kept going, so I had to turn off the circuit breaker at the electrical panel. When I turned the breaker back on, it started again. Upon further inspection, I see that the clear plastic cover on the control panel has “bubbled up” or separated from the door and it appears moisture has gotten behind it into the controls. I tried drying things out with a hair dryer, and I turned the breaker back on. I tried running the dishwasher on a regular cycle and, for the time being, it appears to be working, but the LED display is still showing strange no -number things, and the clear plastic cover is still bubbled up. I will be pursuing a warranty claim with Whirlpool and/or seeking a full replacement (with a different brand! ) from Lowe's.

Sentence (English): We are remodeling our home and replaced all the appliances with Kitchen Aid Appliances.
Comments (English): [ Differences from new to old dishwasher ] || ---------------- || We are remodeling our home and replaced all the appliances with Kitchen Aid Appliances. In rating the dishwasher, I can only compare it to what we had which was a GE dishwasher. Here is a list of some of the things that were not as good as the previous dishwasher.1) The door is very stiff and takes a lot more downward pressure to get the door to totally open.2) The previous dishwasher had the utensil rack in the front of the bottom rack as opposed to along the right side. So, in order to just put some silverware in the rack you have to open the door quite a bit to get them in the back of the rack. When it is in the front it was much easier to just crack open the door and place the silverware.3) When we run the dishwasher on either express wash or normal wash the dishes do not come out dry. Everything is soaking wet in the machine. And express wash does not allow you to select extended dry. We prewash our dishes, so we usually use express wash. When using normal wash, it takes over three hours to do the full load. We have not tried normal wash with extended dry to see if it does a better job with drying the dishes. I now the heater is working, because when we open the door after the machine is done, a lot of steam and hot air comes out the door. We usually wait about 15 minutes with the door open before we unload it.Again, all of the above comments are differences between the new dishwasher and the old dishwasher we had.

Sentence (English): We bought matching Cafe Range, microwave and Dishwasher from Home Depot and selected to get them installed at the time of delivery.
Comments (English): [ Complicated Beauty ] || ---------------- || We bought matching Cafe Range, Microwave and Dishwasher from Home Depot and selected to get them installed at the time of delivery. The Range and Microwave install went perfectly, and both are easy to use. The Dishwasher, however, was not able to be installed at that time. Our previous dishwasher was hardwired and the new Cafe Drawer dishwasher requires a regular electrical outlet. So the next day we had an Electrician install a GFCI outlet, and a Plumber to finish the install. It took the plumber (who is a Master Plumber with 20+ years experience) 5 hours to complete the install. He said the installation instructions were severely lacking in clarity and the water - drain pipes / connections could lead to clogs and draining issues. He modified our plumbing to better accommodate the dishwasher. After the install was complete the dishwasher works great (hense the 4 star rating). The dishwasher drains completely, the Cascade pods dissolve fully, and the dishes come out very clean in both the top and bottom drawers. I think most of the issues experienced with this unit are due to it requiring a specific plumbing set-up. We spent almost as much on the installation (and necessary modifications) than we did for the dishwasher itself. But in the end I am happy with the purchase. It's just my husband and I so the size is perfect. My favorite thing is being able to run just one drawer instead of the full dishwasher. It is also very quiet.Some constructive feedback:1. There should be a Drying option for the Rinse cycle2. There should be an indicator light when the cycle is over3. Better instructions (more detailed / clearer wording) for installers and owners

I now the heater is working, because when we open the door after the machine is done, a lot of steam and hot air comes out the door. We usually wait about 15 minutes with the door open before we unload it. Again, all of the above comments are differences between the new dishwasher and the old dishwasher we had.

Sentence (English): Super bummed about the new machine.
Comments (English): [ Disappointed ] || ---------------- || Super bummed about the new machine. We had a Bosch dishwasher that did fantastic for 17 years and finally control board went. We would have nothing but a Bosch. Decided to get a premium 500 series because of ultraquiet noise level. Super dissapointed. While it is very quiet, the machine feels cheap. The door is flimsy. The plastic latch feels like it will break every time we close the door. The racks slide poorly and the racks are very thin and wobbly. Seems poorly designed and cant get as much in as before. The top 3rd rack is horrible. Hard to believe marketing development suggested people want that, it does nothing but get in the way. Saw some reviews on line that many people removed theirs. Plus its plastic and so it stays wet all the time. Thats part of the beauty of a Bosch with no heating element and stainless steel interior, it defeats the drying with a giant piece of plastic at the top. The ultimate rub is that it doesnt even have a rinse cycle! With all of this home connect smart stuff, i thought we had to access the rinse cycle through the app but yet this premium machine doesnt have one? what the heck. The pairing process for bluetooth to my phone was buggy and took 4 trys.

Sentence (English): Unit works well, quiet as advertised.
Comments (English): [ Very happy with purchase ] || ---------------- || Unit works well, quiet as advertised. I installed it myself and that was simple. I have smart LG washer and dryer which influenced my decision to purchase an LG dishwasher that was smart. Connecting to the app was extremely simple compared to previous version. The middle slide track was defective and spilled ball bearings when I slid the rack out the first time. LG support was helpful and being connected helped because they had all the details regarding model. I just wanted the part and they sent at no charge, easy to install. I've had the unit for a month and my only negative is the middle rack does not maintain horizontal alignment. As I put glasses in the rack it will tip towards the back or front. Consequently I need to compensate when sliding the rack back so it goes all the way in and seats against the water connection for the sprayer. This appears to be a design issue with slack between rack and the track as well as track mounting to the walls with little tabs as opposed to screws.
